Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:10:1.hebrew: רפת שאמרו - ששנינו במשנתנו, עסקינן כשאינה מתעה את הבהמה שבתוכה להיות בורחת ויוצאת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:10:1.english: A stable that they mentioned - [i.e.,] that we learned in our Mishnah; we are dealing [with a case] where it does not cause the animal inside it to stray, fleeing and going out.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:10:2.hebrew: ואינה משתמרת - שאינה נעולה, ואם באת לצאת, יוצאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:10:2.english: And it is not guarded - For [the stable] is not locked, and if [the animal] comes to go out, it goes out.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:11:1.english: [He] brings [it] inside - As we said above (Bava Metzia 31a), "[Returning it] to his garden or to his ruin — from where [do we derive this]?"

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:12:1.hebrew: ברישא גרסינן והוא שעומדת בתוך לתחום. בסיפא גרסינן והוא שעומדת חוץ לתחום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:12:1.english: In the first clause [of the Mishnah], we read: "And that is [only] when it is standing within the [city] limit." In the latter clause, we read: "And that is [only] when it is standing outside the [city] limit."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:14:1.hebrew: אני ה' - אע"פ שאמרתי לך ירא את אביך, אני אדון לשניכם; ואם אמר לך אביך עבור על דברי לחלל שבת, אל תשמע לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:14:1.english: I am the Lord - Even though I said to you, "Fear your father," I am the Master of both of you; and if your father says to you, "Transgress My words to desecrate Shabbat," do not listen to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:15:1.english: I would say [that] he obeys him - For the positive commandment of honoring [one's father] comes and overrides the negative commandment of "you may not hide yourself."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:15:2.hebrew: אבידה, עשה ולא תעשה היא: "השב תשיבם", "לא תוכל להתעלם":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:15:2.english: [Returning] a lost item is a positive commandment and a prohibition: "You shall surely return them," [and] "You may not hide yourself."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:16:1.hebrew: הוקש כבודם - בגזירה שוה: "כבד את אביך", "כבד את ה' מהונך":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:16:1.english: Their honor was equated - Through a gezerah shavah [verbal analogy]: "Honor your father," [and] "Honor the Lord with your wealth."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:19:1.english: Where there is no monetary loss - if one does not load [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:19:2.english: Unloading involves monetary loss - For the animal breaks down under its burden.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:19:3.hebrew: לומר לך פריקה בחנם - אבל טעינה לא נצטוית אלא בשכר. הלכך, אי לא כתב פריקה ואתיא מק"ו מטעינה, הוה אמינא דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון: מה טעינה בשכר, אף פריקה בשכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:19:3.english: To tell you [that] unloading [is performed] for free - However, [with regard to] loading, you were only commanded [to do it] for remuneration. Therefore, if [the Merciful One] had not written [the mitzva of] unloading, and it had been derived through an a fortiori inference from loading, I would have said: It is sufficient for that which is derived [from an inference] to be like the source [from which it is derived] — just as loading [is performed] for remuneration, so too unloading [is performed] for remuneration.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:1:1.english: Two out of three - Two of the three shall come and testify, saying, "We were three."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:20:1.hebrew: לא מסיימי קראי - למשמעות טעינה. הלכך, אי כתיב חד, הוה אמינא לפריקה אתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:20:1.english: The verses are not [clearly] defined - regarding the meaning of loading. Therefore, if [only] one [verse] were written, I would say [that] it came for unloading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:21:1.english: Crouching under its burden - [This] indicates that [one] needs to unload [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:21:2.hebrew: דרמו אינהו וטעונייהו באורחא - אף המשא מוטל על הקרקע, שצריך לטעון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:21:2.english: That they and their burdens are lying on the way - Even the burden is lying on the ground, so that it needs to be loaded.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:2:1.hebrew: אם יש שם ב"ד - וסתם ב"ד שלשה, אלמא אין כח להפקיר ממון זה אצל זה בפחות משלשה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:2:1.english: If there is a court there - And an unspecified court [consists of] three [judges]; thus, there is no authority to render one's money ownerless [in favor of] another with fewer than three.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:3:1.english: Disclosure of the matter - So that they will know that I divided equally.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:3:2.english: A widow - [One who] is sustained from the orphans' property sells [property] for sustenance.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:3:3.hebrew: שלא בב"ד - ובלבד שיראו שנים, שלא תמכור בזול:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:3:3.english: Not before a court - Provided that two [witnesses] see [it], so that she does not sell cheaply.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:5:1.english: [If] he found it in a stable - In the Gemara, it explains why [this ruling] was necessary.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:5:2.english: It was in a graveyard - And he is a priest.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:5:3.english: Or if [his father] said to him: "Do not return [it]" - And it is in a place where he is permitted to go.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:7:1.english: Went and sat down - [This refers to] the owner.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32a:8:1.english: But not to load - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32a:16:1.hebrew: כבד את ה' מהונך - הא דנקט קרא דדברי קבלה, ולא נקט קרא דאיש אמו ואביו תיראו וכתיב את ה' אלהיך תירא — משום דניחא ליה לאתויי קרא דכבוד:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32a:16:1.english: "Honor the Lord with your wealth" - The reason [the Gemara] cited a verse from the Words of Tradition [i.e., Writings], and did not cite the verse "Every man shall fear his mother and his father" while it is written "You shall fear the Lord your God," is because it preferred to bring a verse [speaking] of honor:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32a:3:1.hebrew: אלמנה מוכרת שלא בב"ד - וא"ת: התם משום חינא או משום שלא תתבזה בב"ד, כדמפרש באלמנה ניזונת (כתובות דף צז. ושם)? וי"ל: דס"ל, כיון דאלמנה מוכרת אע"ג דאינה שלה שלא בב"ד משום חינא, ה"נ שותף יטול את שלו שלא בב"ד אע"ג דליכא טעם דחינא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32a:3:1.english: "A widow sells not before a court" - And if you ask: There [she may do so] because of grace [i.e., to make marriage attractive], or so that she will not be humiliated in court, as [the Gemara] explains in [the chapter] Almanah Nizonet (Ketubot 97a and there)? One can answer: [Rav Safra] holds [that] since a widow sells [property] not before a court because of grace even though it is not hers, so too a partner may take what is his not before a court even though there is no reason of grace.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32a:4:1.hebrew: בית דין הדיוטות - וא"ת: והאמרינן התם (דף צח. ושם): "אלמנה ששמה לעצמה לא עשתה ולא כלום, דאמרינן לה: מאן שם לך" — הלא מכרה ע"פ ב"ד הדיוטות! וי"ל: כיון שלוקחת לעצמה, נראה לעולם שמעכבת מנכסי יתומים בידה, אע"פ שיש ב"ד הדיוטות, כיון דליכא מומחין; אבל כשמוכרת לאחרים, אין נראה שמעכבת משלהם, שהרי לא עכבה כלום. וא"ת: ומ"ש דאלמנה מוכרת לאחרים שלא בב"ד, ובב"ד יכולה לעכב אפי' לעצמה — מדאמרינן התם דא"ל "מאן שם לך", משמע דבב"ד יכולה לשום; וקאמר נמי התם: "ההוא גברא דאפקידו גביה כסתא דיתמי, אזל שמה לנפשיה בת' זוזי, לסוף אייקור כו', אתא לקמיה דרבי, א"ל: מאן שם לך", משמע דבב"ד יכול לשום. ולקמן בפרק המפקיד (בבא מציעא דף לח.) תנן: "המפקיד פירות אצל חבירו והרקיבו כו', עושה להם תקנה ומוכרן בב"ד", וכשהוא מוכרן — מוכרן לאחרים ואין מוכרן לעצמו. כיוצא בו: "גבאי צדקה פורטין לאחרים ואין פורטין לעצמם", דאפילו בב"ד מוכרין לאחרים ואין מוכרין לעצמם, ושלא בב"ד אין מוכרין אפילו לאחרים. וליכא למימר הא דאמר "ומוכרים לאחרים בב"ד" היינו ברשות ב"ד, אבל אי ידעי ב"ד השומא יכול לעכב לעצמו — דבירושלמי מסיק על ההוא מעשה דרבי יוחנן חקוקאה, דמייתי פ"ק דפסחים (דף יג. ושם): א"ל "לך ומוכרם בב"ד", אלמא אע"פ שנתן לו רשות, היה צריך למוכרם בב"ד! וי"ל: דמוכרת שלא בב"ד משום חינא. וגבי כסתא דיתמי נמי דיכול לעכב לעצמו בב"ד, מצינן למימר דהיינו דוקא בדיעבד, דמשום חשד לא מהדרינן עובדא; א"נ, דגבי יתמי ב"ד עצמם הם מפקידין, ולכך יכול לעכב לעצמו על פיהם, אבל פקדון של אחרים אינו יכול לעכב לעצמו על פי ב"ד:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32a:4:1.english: A court of laymen - And if you will say: Didn't we say there (Ketubot 98a and elsewhere): "A widow who appraised [estate property] for herself has done nothing, for we say to her: 'Who appraised [it] for you?'" — [yet] wasn't her sale [carried out] through a court of laymen?! And one can answer: Since she is taking [it] for herself, it appears to everyone that she is withholding [value] from the orphans' property in her hand, even though there is a court of laymen, since there are no experts; however, when she sells to others, it does not appear that she is withholding from theirs, for she has withheld nothing. And if you will say: What is the difference [between a widow and others], that a widow sells to others without a court, and with a court she can withhold [property] even for herself — from what we say there, that we say to her "Who appraised [it] for you?", it implies that with a court she can appraise [for herself]; and it also says there: "A certain man with whom was deposited coral belonging to orphans went [and] appraised it for himself at four hundred zuz; eventually it appreciated, etc.; he came before Rabbi [Ammi], [and] he said to him: 'Who appraised [it] for you?'", which implies that with a court he can appraise [for himself]. And later, in the chapter [entitled] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 38a), we learned in a Mishnah: "One who deposits produce with his fellow and it rotted, etc., he makes an arrangement for them and sells them in court", and when he sells them, he sells them to others and does not sell them to himself. Similarly: "Charity collectors change [coins] for others and do not change [them] for themselves", for even with a court they sell to others and do not sell to themselves, and without a court they do not sell even to others. And one cannot say [that] what it states, "and they sell to others in court", means with the permission of the court, but if the court knows the appraisal he may withhold [it] for himself — for in the Jerusalem Talmud it concludes regarding that incident of Rabbi Yochanan Chakuka'ah, which is brought in the first chapter of Pesachim (13a and elsewhere): he said to him, "Go and sell them in court"; thus, even though he gave him permission, he was required to sell them in court! And one can answer: That she sells without a court is because of [the concern for] favor [so that she will find favor and remarry]. And regarding the coral of the orphans as well, that he can withhold [it] for himself with a court, we can say that this is specifically ex post facto [bedi'avad], for because of suspicion we do not reverse the transaction; or alternatively, regarding orphans, the court themselves are the ones who deposit [the property], and therefore he can withhold [it] for himself at their direction, whereas a deposit of others he cannot withhold for himself through a court.
